subject: computer-science
title: Worst, Best, Average and Amortised
welcome_lead: Different ways to measure how an algorithm really behaves.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: worst-case, best-case, average-case and amortised analysis.
final_note: Always know which case a Big-O figure refers.

concepts.def: The largest running time over all inputs of size n.
The smallest running time over all inputs of size n.
Expected running time over a distribution of inputs.
Average cost per operation over a long sequence.
Tight bound — same upper and lower asymptotic growth.

walkthroughs.body_html: Linear search has best case O(1) (target first), worst case O(n) (not present), average case about O(n/2). Quoting Big O usually means worst case unless stated.
Appending to a dynamic array is O(1) amortised — most appends are cheap, with occasional O(n) resizes. Averaged over many operations, the cost per append is constant.
Big Omega is a lower bound; Big Theta is a tight bound. Merge sort is Theta(n log n) — both upper and lower bounded by n log n.

mcqs.q: What is the time complexity of binary search?
options: Writing code that does not work.
O(n) - because it searches through items.
O(log n).
O(1) - because it is fast.

mcqs.q: What is abstraction in computer science?
options: Writing code that does not work.
Making something abstract art or vague.
O(1) - because it is fast.
Removing unnecessary detail to focus on essential features of a problem.
